title: See Me Now, the crazy trombonist who followed the show
summary: Love tells about a canvas man on a Mississippi tent show nicknamed See Me Now who bought a trombone and kept beating the show to the next town.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: We had a fella in Mississippi, we used to call him See Me Now. You know, why we give him that name? You know, comedian fellas is funny, you know. They see fellas do something funny and they make something out of it. This fella come up one day, they used to get passes, you see. Bring their sweetheart to the show or something like that. You get a pass, you could bring his gun, you see. Well, this was one of the canvas boys, you know. People was kind of scared of him too, said he was a fool. He always was fooling around in the grass with some kind of weed, you know. And he'd break a piece and put it in his pocketbook. And everybody on the show scared of him. So he come up to the boys one evening and say, I want a pass, I want two passes. I got some friends I want to bring them to the show tonight, see me now? And the boys looked at him, said you better get away from here, you crazy. He said, that's all I got to sell is tickets. I'm going to give you some tickets. He said, you know, I'll bring my girl out. Girl, see me now? So we laughed at him so much that we just call him, see me now, you see. We go on out with the show. So the boys got sick of this fella, you know. Some of them show people bleeding that stuff too, and the boys himself, come as to bleeding, see me now, was bad luck, you see. So we put Seaman off the show. What made him put them off? He was like silly, you know, crazy. He seen Earl Offred playing trombone, you know, and Earl used to play loud trombone, you know. And he was working putting up the tent, helping them fellas put up the tent. So he went to town and he just had a payday, you know, took his last money, some pawn shop, and got a trombone, bought himself a trombone. And he never had a lesson in his life. He couldn't play, you know. He come back down there, he seen the musicians getting all fine, you know. The boys come up and say, hey, them fellas looking for you, you better go help put up that tent. He said, from now on I ain't putting up no tent, I'm going to play trombone in the dance. The boys said, I know you crazy now. So he went up under the tent after the fellas put the tent up and was watching all around there. I pop up, I make no kind of noise, you know. When the band went out that day, he tried to follow the band. So dear to dear
See we're talking about Simi Now, you say he played trombone with the band even though

he never had a lesson. No, they didn't let him play. So they got the towel down, the boy seen him losing, thought he was going crazy. He told Simi Now, everybody was scared of him, they thought he was a hoodoo or something. So he told the policeman, that's a pretty good fellow, we don't want you to put him in there and keep him in there now. I said, but I want you to run one thing, he's following this show and you want to get rid of him. He said, you just arrest him and lock him up, tell this show get out of town. When he get out of town, you turn him loose. You turn him loose and let him go. He hasn't done anything, bothered anybody on the show. I think he's a good boy too, he said, but we don't want to carry him around like this. So the police done like he told him, took the boy and put him in jail on the show, got out of town. They turned him loose and he didn't know where the show was going. When we got in the next town, Simi Now was sitting on a bridge, you know, up on the railing, waving at the people. And they went to the show lot and putting up the tents, Simi Now was right there. And several times there wouldn't nobody tell him where we was going, you know, try to shake. And he would be in the town before the show get there. And how he get there, I don't know. But anyway, the boss put the police on him and told the police, he said, you keep him here three days and I know we won't see him no more. He said, turn him loose after three days. He was following the show and we don't want him with the show. Well, after he kept him three days and the show went on, we lost him. We didn't know where the show was at. But that's his state, you know, he must have known his state because every time they're leaving, he'd beat the show to the other town.
